review: FIRST independent desktop display review only

observations.observation: The heading 'Electric circuits — conductors in series and in parallel' is fully visible on one line. The English chapter breadcrumb wraps cleanly to 'Printed page 214' without colliding with the heading or prose. The centered reading column has wide side margins, readable body text, and consistent line and paragraph spacing.

Thin horizontal rules and bold English labels clearly separate Series connection, Parallel connection, Measuring current, and Measuring voltage. Rules remain within the reading column and do not cross text or figures.

English prose wraps within the column without visible truncation or overlap. Inline resistance and current subscripts are visible. The displayed relations I_1 = I_2 = I, V = V_1 + V_2, R = R_1 + R_2, I = I_1 + I_2, 1/R = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2, R = R_1 R_2/(R_1 + R_2), and R' = R R_0/(R + R_0) < R have visible mathematical glyphs and fraction bars. Equation numbers (9-6) through (9-10) occupy separate lines without colliding with formulas or prose. This is a rendering observation, not a renewed science review.

All four figures are centered within the reading column beside their relevant explanatory passages. English captions Figure 173, Figure 174, Figure 175, and Figure 176 appear centered beneath their respective diagrams, lighter and smaller than body text but legible. There is clear separation between diagrams, captions, and following paragraphs.

The two resistor rectangles, node dots, current arrow, and dotted voltage-span arrows are crisp and fully contained. R_1, R_2, I, V_1, and V_2 remain distinct; subscripts are visible and labels do not intersect the circuit lines.

Both branches, resistor rectangles, junction dots, and dotted central voltage span are fully visible. The a and b junction labels, I, I_1, I_2, R_1, R_2, and V are readable and separated from their nearby wires and arrows. The bottom I_2 subscript is present and not cut off.

The ammeter circle and its centered A, the resistor rectangle and its R label, and the horizontal conductor are sharp and unclipped. White space separates the diagram from its surrounding prose and caption.

The upper resistor, two junction dots, lower voltmeter branch, and circular V symbol are fully visible. R and V are clearly readable with no wire crossing the letters, and the diagram has adequate margins.

No visible overlapping prose, captions, circuit labels, replacement boxes, missing mathematical glyphs, or horizontally clipped content was observed. Figure 173 continues below the bottom of the 960-pixel introductory viewport as normal document scrolling; the whole-page and figure screenshots show the complete diagram. The final prose is present above the bottom page margin.

limitations: PASS applies only to the six supplied desktop display images for phy9-c2-s3-n93, rendered at desktop viewport 1440x960. No mobile, source, or other images were opened; no image was reopened or cropped, and no image payload is returned.

This is an isolated headless offline display review only, not live DB verification, live product or production verification, or headed acceptance. No browser session, network request, publication, database operation, or paid call was performed by this review.

The whole-page screenshot is 1440x7359 and was automatically resized by functions.view_image to 1174x6000 for inspection. The separate introductory viewport and four figure screenshots supplement that overview. No new crops or enlarged views were made; complete native-size glyph certification for every prose line is not claimed.

The source-bound Chinese machine ARIA/alt identity is retained and disclosed, not translated or certified here. The desktop report explicitly records Chinese figure ARIA labels for Figures 173 through 176 and sets completeEnglishAccessibilityApproval to false. Pixels cannot establish alternative-text quality or screen-reader behavior; this is not full English accessibility certification.

Existing source, science, and diagram reviews remain valid and were not redone. This review judges visible placement, readability, separators, captions, and rendering defects only, not source fidelity, scientific correctness, circuit topology approval, or complete-course acceptance.
